newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Black group seeks control of S.Africa's Gold Fields.
newsitem.headline: Black group seeks control of S.Africa's Gold Fields.

text.p: Black empowerment group New Africa Investment Ltd (Nail) said on Thursday it was in talks to take joint control of Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd, the world's third largest gold producer.

Nail, headed by former African National Congress secretary-general Cyril Ramaphosa, aims to buy an effective 17.2 percent stake in the mining group, giving it joint control with Rembrandt Group Ltd which already owns a similar stake.

The deal, if successful, would mark a further big advance for black business in South Africa -- and a significant coup for Nail which already has control of industrial group Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd.
Gold Fields would provide a major presence in the mining industry, a key goal for Nail.

Nail had been seen as a potential bidder for a stake in rival mining house JCI Ltd, but that deal was finally clinched by another black empowerment consortium, African Mining Group, led by Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd.

Nail hopes to acquire from Gold Fields and its Driefontein Consolidated Ltd unit their 40 percent shareholding in Asteroid Ltd. Asteroid holds 40 percent of GFSA Holdings Ltd which, in turn, holds 43 percent of Gold Fields.
"The successful conclusion of these discussions would result in a partnership being formed between Rembrandt Group Ltd and Nail in GFSA Holdings Ltd," it said in a brief statement.
Based on current market prices, the deal could be worth more than 1.8 billion rand ($400 million).
Rembrandt already holds 40 percent of GFSA Holdings. The addition of a similar holding by Nail would give the two partners 34.4 percent control of Gold Fields.

Gold Fields -- whose future has been subject of speculation for months -- produced 23.45 tonnes of gold in the quarter to end-March when it made an after-tax profit of 236.42 million rand before capital expenditure.
